decisions: Use one canonical cross-platform repository-relative lexical path contract; allow legitimate dotfiles/hidden paths but reject .git metadata, traversal, absolute paths, backslashes and obvious Windows-invalid names.
Use sorted unique exact repository file paths for V1 MutationDeclaration and bind the declaration to the exact Standard Action Run occurrence; do not introduce glob/regex/path-policy selectors now.
Evaluate observed repository candidate paths deterministically against the declaration; any observed out-of-scope path blocks mutation/checkpoint progression.
Reuse Policy READY_CHECKPOINT_EVALUATION as the lifecycle checkpoint seam rather than duplicating Archive ordering.
Keep checkpoint eligibility separate from explicit Owner checkpoint authorization and from actual Git execution.
Reuse existing OwnerAuthorityFact and require exact decision=authorize-checkpoint, exact Delivery/Change and scope=[checkpoint] at the semantic checkpoint boundary.
Treat Verification/check evidence as eligibility evidence only; it never creates mutation or Git authority.
Leave OpenSpec artifact observation, Git command execution, CLI surface and cross-platform whole-manager acceptance to their already-planned later Changes.
limitations: The supplied checkpoint snapshot has no .git metadata, so base Git revision 8c0c150b4bd15e837c3f579a91e0303678fbbe4b cannot be independently verified inside this detached snapshot.
The focused Git observation proof ran on Linux; Windows Native parity remains for the final cross-platform acceptance Change.
The V1 repository path contract is lexical and does not establish symlink/junction/reparse containment hardening or a generic filesystem writer API.
Formal OpenSpec-derived mutation declaration generation and actual Git commit orchestration are deferred to the planned thin-integration and CLI Changes.
nonGoals: Git wrapper CLI or automatic git add/commit/push/merge/tag
Verification evidence registry or path-to-test permission engine
generic filesystem sandbox or symlink/junction hardening framework
